summary: Claude loaded the hyperpowers:brainstorming skill, read the repo (find/cat of pyproject, README, ADR, all src and test files) before asking anything, asked only decision questions (formats, destination, JSON schema, format selection), presented a design in chat and stopped for approval without writing code (git status clean).
reasoning: All six acceptance criteria are supported by session-log evidence: the brainstorming skill was loaded natively, repo investigation preceded the first question, all questions were genuine decisions (I never used the 'check the repo' reply), and the agent presented a design and halted with the working tree unchanged. The only blemish is that overwrite behavior was assumed rather than asked, which is a design-quality observation, not a criterion failure.

observations.description: The agent did not ask about overwrite behavior — a decision the story lists as mine. It unilaterally chose 'Overwrite silently, like shell >', which is the opposite of the intended answer (fail unless --force). It did flag it as 'Behaviors I'm choosing, flag them if any is wrong', so it's an assumption surfaced rather than hidden, but it was decided rather than asked.
Several questions came as an interactive picker (AskUserQuestion) while one (destination) came as plain chat prose with no picker — inconsistent interaction mode within the same conversation.

The agent mentioned an internal implementation detail to the user: 'Codex is on PATH, but I'm skipping the Codex approach gate here', and ran a Bash cat of the skill's codex-approach-gate.md. Leaky for an end user.

The agent's recommendation on the first question (plain text only) contradicted the user's stated goal framing; it required me to use 'Type something' to say CSV+JSON since option 3 was 'Text + CSV + JSON' with no CSV+JSON-only option.
Claude Code first-run gauntlet (theme picker, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) requires 4 confirmations before any work; noise for automated/eval runs.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use list, first entry: `Skill :: {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}` (5c55dd58-...jsonl)

All four AskUserQuestion calls in the log were decisions: 'What should `export` be able to write?', 'How should the export destination be specified?', 'What shape should the JSON export have?', 'How should `export` determine the output format?'. I never had to reply 'You can check the repo for that.' No REPO-ANSWERABLE items recorded.

Tool order in log: Skill, then Bash `find . -type f ... && git log`, Bash `cat pyproject.toml README.md deploy/crontab docs/adr/0002-storage-backend.md`, Bash `cat src/reportkit/cli.py ... tests/test_summarize.py`, and only then the first AskUserQuestion. Opening reply also said 'Context read: reportkit is a small Click CLI (summarize --day) over a PostgreSQL store ... ADR-0002 pins PostgreSQL'.

criteria.criterion: Every question was a decision only I can make
criteria.evidence: Four questions asked, all judgment calls (formats CSV/JSON/PDF, --out vs --out-dir, JSON payload schema, explicit --format vs extension inference). None asked about language, test runner, storage backend, existing subcommands, or output format — it had read those.

criteria.criterion: Presented design and stopped for approval
criteria.evidence: Design section '## Design: `reportkit export`' ending 'Does this look right? I'll wait for your go-ahead before writing any code.'; after my reply: 'Understood — stopping here. Nothing written'. `git status --short` in the workdir returned no modified files.

criteria.criterion: Harness-agnostic: shell or native tool evidence counts
criteria.evidence: Investigation was via shell Bash `find`/`cat` calls plus a native Skill call; both forms present in the log and accepted.
